blocks.raw: # Jump
blocks.text: Jump

blocks.raw: The jump functionality allows brands to connect multiple journeys. Some of the salient features of JUmp block are:
blocks.text: The jump functionality allows brands to connect multiple journeys. Some of the salient features of JUmp block are:

blocks.raw:
* Allows marketing team to simplify their journey-designing process
* Eliminates the redundancy of creating the same flows within multiple journeys by allowing users to jump from one journey to another if they meet certain conditions.
* Through personalized journeys, you can ensure customer retention and satisfaction.
* Avoids the complications of creating a complex journey in a single flow and thus simplifies creating hyper-personalized journeys.
* Avoids monotony creating similar flows within each journey separately and saves time.

blocks.raw: ## Use Cases
blocks.text: Use Cases

blocks.raw: Assume that a brand wants to give customers who spend more than $100 in their store 500 bonus points and certain other incentives. If a customer spends more than $500 in Journey A, they will jump to Journey B (elite customers) which includes customers that have a free membership + incentives. The brand can include a Jump activity within their journey A that caters to the value of a transaction.

blocks.raw: ## Configuring a jump block

blocks.raw:
1. Drag and drop the **Jump** block to the end of the path on the journey canvas. Whenever a user reaches this block, they will be directed to a different journey as per the configuration in the Jump block.
2. Click on the **Jump** block in the canvas.

4. From the drop-down, select the desired existing journey. You can also use the search box and search for a particular journey.  You can click on the info icon and  view the summary of the selected journey
5. Click **Done**

blocks.raw: The Issue Incentive block allows you to reward customers during their journey without sending a communication. This helps brands that run multiple offers or incentives avoid spamming customers with excessive notifications.
blocks.text: The Issue Incentive block allows you to reward customers during their journey without sending a communication. This helps brands that run multiple offers or incentives avoid spamming customers with excessive notifications.

blocks.raw: You can issue <Anchor label="offers" target="_blank" href="https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/create-offer-1#/create-offers">offers</Anchor>, <Anchor label="points" target="_blank" href="https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/points#/">points</Anchor>, <Anchor label="cart promotions" target="_blank" href="https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/create-cart-promotion#/">cart promotions</Anchor>, <Anchor label="gift vouchers" target="_blank" href="https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/configure-a-gift-voucher#/">gift vouchers</Anchor>, [badges](https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/enabling-creating-a-badge#/), and <Anchor label="loyalty promotions" target="_blank" href="https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/loyalty-promotions#/">loyalty promotions</Anchor> using this block.

blocks.raw:
* **Points**, **cart promotions**, **gift vouchers**, and **loyalty promotions** must be created before you can add them as incentives.
* **Offers** and **badges** can be created while issuing the incentive.

  **Note**: **Loyalty promotions** are not enabled by default. Raise a Jira ticket to the PST team to get it enabled for your organization.

blocks.raw: # Webhook
blocks.text: Webhook

blocks.raw: The webhook block enables your Journeys to send and receive information in real-time through a webhook. You can use this block to capture specific details during a customer journey and send them to external third-party systems for further processing.
blocks.text: The webhook block enables your Journeys to send and receive information in real-time through a webhook. You can use this block to capture specific details during a customer journey and send them to external third-party systems for further processing.

blocks.raw: For example, if you use an external service to issue coupons, you can configure the journey to trigger their webhook when a specific event occurs, such as a customer completing a purchase. The event data is sent to the external service through their webhook, and the service then processes the information independently to issue a coupon to the customer.
blocks.text: For example, if you use an external service to issue coupons, you can configure the journey to trigger their webhook when a specific event occurs, such as a customer completing a purchase. The event data is sent to the external service through their webhook, and the service then processes the information independently to issue a coupon to the customer.

blocks.raw: The webhook block supports POST and PUT HTTP methods. You can configure it with [query parameters](https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/action-building-block#/query-parameters), [headers](https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/action-building-block#headers), and a [JSON payload](https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/action-building-block#payload-request-body) to send data to external systems.

blocks.raw: ## Webhook request structure
blocks.text: Webhook request structure

blocks.raw: The webhook supports POST and PUT HTTP methods and also supports query parameters, headers and the JSON payload.
blocks.text: The webhook supports POST and PUT HTTP methods and also supports query parameters, headers and the JSON payload.

blocks.raw: ### Query parameters
blocks.text: Query parameters

blocks.raw: Query parameters are simple key-value pairs appended to the end of a URL. They provide visible, top-level context about the request and are ideal for passing simple metadata that helps the external system identify or filter the request.
blocks.text: Query parameters are simple key-value pairs appended to the end of a URL. They provide visible, top-level context about the request and are ideal for passing simple metadata that helps the external system identify or filter the request.

blocks.raw: You can map journey data to query parameters using <Anchor label="labels" target="_blank" href="https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/supported-labels-for-engagement-channels#/">labels</Anchor> or static text. For example, if the query parameter is customerName, you can map it to the label Customer First Name to dynamically pass the customer’s name.
blocks.text: You can map journey data to query parameters using labels or static text. For example, if the query parameter is customerName, you can map it to the label Customer First Name to dynamically pass the customer’s name.

blocks.raw: The external system can then use this information as needed. For instance, if the webhook triggers an external email service, it can use the customer name to personalise the message, for example, addressing the customer as Hi `{{first_name}}`.
blocks.text: The external system can then use this information as needed. For instance, if the webhook triggers an external email service, it can use the customer name to personalise the message, for example, addressing the customer as Hi {{first_name}}.

blocks.raw: ### Headers
blocks.text: Headers

blocks.raw: Headers provide technical instructions and metadata for the receiving server on how to process an incoming request.
blocks.text: Headers provide technical instructions and metadata for the receiving server on how to process an incoming request.

blocks.raw: Use headers for authentication and for specifying the data format. For example, use the `Authorization` header to securely pass an API key or bearer token. Use the `Content-Type` header with a value like `application/json` to inform the server that the payload is structured as JSON.
blocks.text: Use headers for authentication and for specifying the data format. For example, use the Authorization header to securely pass an API key or bearer token. Use the Content-Type header with a value like application/json to inform the server that the payload is structured as JSON.

blocks.raw: ### Payload (request body)
blocks.text: Payload (request body)

blocks.raw: The payload, also referred to as the request body, is the main content of the message. It contains detailed, structured information for the external system to process, especially when using POST or PUT methods.

The payload is generally used to send complex, multi-field, or sensitive data.

blocks.raw: For example, when creating a support ticket, the payload can include the customer’s email address, ticket subject, and comments, all structured within a JSON body. The external system then processes this information to create the support ticket.

blocks.raw: ## Configuring authorization
blocks.text: Configuring authorization

blocks.raw: The **Authorization** tab allows you to specify the credentials the webhook will use. The correct method depends on the requirements of the third-party service. The following types are supported:
blocks.text: The Authorization tab allows you to specify the credentials the webhook will use. The correct method depends on the requirements of the third-party service. The following types are supported:

blocks.raw:
* **None**: No authorisation.
* **Basic Auth**: A simple username and password combination.
* **API Key**: A unique key that you pass in either the headers or parameters. For example, a header named `X-API-Key` with your key as the value.

blocks.raw: ## FAQs
blocks.text: FAQs

blocks.raw:
1. Which HTTP methods are supported?
   The webhook block supports POST and PUT methods.
2. What authentication methods are supported?
   The webhook block supports basic authorization.
3. How many headers or params can I add?
   You can add up to 10 headers and 10 params per request.
4. What happens if I add unsupported tags in the request?
   The request returns a 400 error, and the UI displays an error message stating that the tags are not supported.
5. Does editing a webhook block in a live journey create a new version of the journey?
   Yes. Editing a block in a live journey creates a new version, which then enters the approval flow.
6. Can I edit the configuration once the journey has been sent for approval?
   The webhook block cannot be edited once the journey has been sent for approval. To make changes, reject the approval request and make the changes.
